Why go: Samui's classic sights in one day, without the animal stops

Many island safaris on Koh Samui still include monkey or snake shows. This one does not, and it covers the full list of sights first-time visitors ask about. The morning loops round the north-east: the Big Buddha, the colourful Wat Plai Laem with its many-armed Guan Yin statue, the Hin Ta and Hin Yai rocks and the Guan Yu shrine. After a swim at the first Na Muang waterfall and a look at rubber tapping and coconut processing, the 4x4 climbs into the hills for lunch, the Secret Buddha Garden and the viewpoint at Wat Teepangkorn.

The 4x4 earns its place in the afternoon: the roads to the garden and viewpoint are too steep for a minivan.

Who it suits, and who should choose something else

  • Good for: first-time visitors, families with children from about 4, and anyone without a car or scooter.
  • Choose something else if you want to drive yourself: a Polaris ATV safari reaches the same hills under your own power.
  • Short of time: the Big Buddha and Wat Plai Laem are 10 minutes from Chaweng and easy to visit alone.

Good to know

  • Dress code: the temples require covered shoulders and knees. Bring a sarong rather than changing clothes all day.
  • Open truck: you sit in the back of an open 4x4. It is breezy and fun, but bring a light layer if it rains.
  • Waterfall: the rocks at Na Muang are slippery and people are injured there every year. Swim only where the guide shows you.
  • November: the wettest month on Samui. The tour runs, but expect showers.
